decisions.reason: As a close-to-core semi-hard cheese in a growing dairy market, it likely fits the firm's narrow organic assortment and uses existing capabilities efficiently, so management would usually retain it unless sales clearly disappoint.

The spicy cheese extends the established cheese range but is more niche in taste, so it carries a higher pruning risk than staple cheeses, though it is still close enough to the core business to merit staying on the market for now.

A mild creamy soft cheese suits broad consumer preferences and the firm's healthy, enjoyable organic positioning, making it a plausible long-term assortment item rather than an obvious candidate for withdrawal.
